finding.claim: The ban endpoint performs the ban for non-admin callers. The admin check's 403 is caught by a broad except and the handler continues to do_ban(uid).
finding.source: Any POST to /admin/users/<uid>/ban where g.user is a non-admin user. The uid comes from the URL path (admin.py:15) and is not validated.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, a protected administrative operation. Returns ok=True at admin.py:21.

trace.note: POST route /admin/users/<uid>/ban is registered with no auth decorator in this file
require_admin(g.user) is called inside a try block
require_admin checks user.get('is_admin'); a non-admin fails this check
except Exception catches the HTTPException, since it subclasses Exception, so the 403 is swallowed
log.warning records the failure, then execution falls through with no return or re-raise
do_ban(uid) runs for the non-admin caller
response is jsonify(ok=True), so the attacker sees success

finding.guards_checked: (1) require_admin is_admin check (admin.py:10): works, but its result is discarded by the except at admin.py:18. (2) abort(403) (admin.py:11): raises as intended, but is swallowed at admin.py:18. (3) No return or re-raise after the except block (admin.py:18-19): the handler continues. (4) unban route (admin.py:24-28) calls require_admin without a try block, so its 403 is enforced; the ban route is the outlier. (5) Authentication that sets g.user is not in this file and could not be verified. If g.user is None, the log line at admin.py:19 raises AttributeError and the request fails before do_ban runs, but that is an accident of the error path, not a control. (6) do_ban body (admin.py:31-32) is a stub (pass), so real impact depends on its implementation elsewhere.

verdict.guard_found: The only guard is require_admin (admin.py:9-11), which calls abort(403). Its call at admin.py:17 is inside try/except Exception at admin.py:18-19 with no return or re-raise, so the 403 is swallowed and do_ban(uid) runs at admin.py:20. The unban route (admin.py:26) calls require_admin outside any try block, which confirms the ban route is the outlier. No effective control exists in this file. Authentication that sets g.user is not in this file and could not be checked, but it would only require a logged-in user, not an admin.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20, require_admin's abort(403) is an HTTPException (a subclass of Exception), which the bare except at admin.py:18 swallows before do_ban(uid) runs unconditionally, so any authenticated non-admin can ban users via POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban (returning ok=True at admin.py:21). The stub body of do_ban (admin.py:31-32) means the real-world impact is unverified, but the authorization bypass itself is confirmed.
